clue.text: See 10
A big block of something goes to your head, on the little boat–which is fine!

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: a hunk is a big chunk of something

indicators.note: the head of the word your is its first letter

parts.note: only the head, the opening letter, of this word is used
a dory is a small flat-bottomed rowing boat

explanation.surface: A heavy block lands on your head while you sit in a dinghy, and somehow all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunky-dory is informal for satisfactory, everything being fine and in order.

clue.text: The enclosed part of a plane can bring it up, with how you term a young lady in Paris.

definitions.text: The enclosed part of a plane

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: the word can is used as written, then turned upside down

parts.words: how you term a young lady in Paris
parts.note: elle is French for she, the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Something about a plane's cabin, a can and how Parisians address women.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing on an aircraft that encloses an engine.

clue.text: See 25 across
Could be someone like Noah, but the inventor of a 12 had a different handle.

definitions.text: Could be someone like Noah, but the inventor of a 12 had a different handle.

parts.note: read literally, Noah was a maker of an ark, and a wright is a maker, so an ark-maker fits the word

parts.words: the inventor of a 12 had a different handle
parts.note: 12 is JENNY; the spinning jenny was invented by James Hargreaves, not by the famous textile inventor Richard of this surname, so its inventor had another name (handle)

explanation.surface: A musing on Noah, with an aside that a famous inventor went by some other name.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as ARK + WRIGHT: a wright is a maker, so Noah was literally one. Richard Arkwright was the textile pioneer, but the spinning jenny at 12 was Hargreaves's, hence a different handle.
explanation.definitionFit: An arkwright, taken literally, is a builder of arks, and Noah is the Bible's only famous ark builder.

clue.text: The USA is wrong when a tree is chopped to pieces by it, which is very plain!

indicators.note: USA is wrong, so its letters must be put in a different order

parts.note: the three letters of USA are taken as written and jumbled

indicators.note: a tree chopped to pieces has its letters broken up and reassembled

parts.note: the word tree is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that America is wrong to cut down trees, leaving a bare landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Plain looks like a flat landscape after the felling; here it means unadorned.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severely simple and without ornament, so very plain.

clue.text: They provide a certain amount of cover in Japan, with a Kipling character soon troubled by it.

definitions.text: They provide a certain amount of cover in Japan

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel Kim

indicators.note: soon is troubled, stirred up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word soon is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Japanese coverings, and Kipling's boy hero soon distressed by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kimonos are the long robes traditionally worn in Japan, covering much of the body.

clue.text: Where some people fight to see what might be on your finger.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the roped arena for boxing or wrestling

definitions.text: what might be on your finger
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a band of metal worn as jewellery

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves picture a boxing match and a wedding band, two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a boxing arena and a piece of jewellery worn on a finger.

clue.text: If this is in the works, you'll do badly in the Graduate Record Exam–get 1,000 to zero coming on up…

definitions.text: If this is in the works, you'll do badly
definitions.note: a description standing for the noun: the thing which, in the works, makes you fail

parts.note: the GRE is the American admissions test for graduate school
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word coming up reads from bottom to top

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A warning that you will score badly on a graduate entrance test.
explanation.walkthrough: In the works means in the machinery: a gremlin is the imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults, not a bad exam result.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is the mischievous imp blamed for unexplained mechanical breakdowns, spoiling the machinery.

clue.text: …and at coming up on a pigpen, you could still consider this very palatable.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
in a down clue, a word coming up reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the word at is taken as written and turned upside down
a sty is an enclosure for pigs

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: even food served above a pigsty might still taste good.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasty food is delicious, very pleasant to eat.

clue.text: The heart of things, but Uncle is wrong to go to the country.

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters go to, that is are joined by, the next piece placed after them
when the word Uncle is wrong its letters are out of order and need rearranging

parts.note: the word Uncle is taken as written and its letters jumbled
US is the usual abbreviation for the United States, the country

explanation.surface: An uncle makes a mistake by emigrating, though the clue opens by talking about the core of matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleus is the central core around which something is built, so it is the heart of things.

clue.text: Fools around with "Fatha." (Such are pretty tricky!)

definitions.note: a description standing for the plural noun: things of this kind are tricks and pranks

parts.note: to monkey around is to fool about, so he fools around becomes he monkeys
Earl "Fatha" Hines was a celebrated American jazz pianist, known by that nickname

explanation.surface: Someone clowns about with a jazz legend, and the parenthesis warns that such antics are tricky.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two lights: 10-across takes the first seven letters and 1-across, clued only as 'See 10', takes the last five.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkeyshines is an American word for mischievous tricks or pranks, which is exactly what tricky things are.

clue.text: You at first take to drink in school.

indicators.note: the first piece is taken to, that is joined onto, the drink that follows
only the opening letter of the word You is wanted here

parts.note: only the opening letter of this word is used
ale is beer, a common drink

explanation.surface: Advice that a student should take up drinking while at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a famous American Ivy League university, which counts as a school in US usage.

clue.text: The female of certain species, but it's just a sail for the tar.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the female of the donkey or the wren is called a ...

definitions.text: just a sail for the tar
definitions.meaning: second meaning: to a sailor (a tar) a ... is a genoa jib, a large headsail

explanation.walkthrough: Tar is old slang for a sailor, so 'for the tar' marks the sailing jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a female donkey or wren, and in yachting slang it is short for the big genoa foresail.

clue.text: Quiet, Myrna! It's only a stratagem!

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning play quietly
Myrna Loy was a Hollywood film star of the 1930s

explanation.surface: Someone tells actress Myrna to hush because what is going on is just a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a cunning manoeuvre or tactic, the same as a stratagem.

clue.text: A graceful swimmer found in an unusual backup of water overseas.

definitions.text: an unusual backup of water overseas
definitions.note: the place name stands for its famous dam, which backs up the Nile into a huge reservoir

parts.note: the word A is taken as written
the swan is the classic image of a graceful bird gliding on water

explanation.surface: A swan discovered gliding on some strange overflow abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Aswan is a city in southern Egypt; its High Dam holds back the Nile to form Lake Nasser.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aswan High Dam in Egypt impounds the Nile, one of the world's largest artificial reservoirs.

clue.text: After war breaks out, most of the answer is complete rage!

indicators.note: the shortened word comes after the rearranged letters
war breaks out, so its letters break apart and re-form in a new order

parts.note: the word war is taken as written and its letters jumbled

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it except its last letter

parts.note: the word the is taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: When war erupts, the answer is mostly fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense anger, rage in full measure.

clue.text: Look after things, hearing that one is on another continent.

indicators.note: hearing a phrase means taking its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: someone on another continent is abroad, beyond the sea

explanation.surface: Minding things while picturing someone away on a distant continent.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or manage, which is looking after things.

clue.text: Worn in some places in the East–with a right to have words and music around.

definitions.text: Worn in some places in the East

indicators.note: the songs are to have the other letters, that is hold them
the songs go around the short pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: songs combine lyrics and a tune
the word a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Eastern clothing linked somehow with the right to compose lyrics and tunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarongs are wrapped cloth skirts worn in South and Southeast Asia, garments of the East.

clue.text: Five hundred times as sweet as sugar!

definitions.text: Five hundred times as sweet as sugar!

parts.note: a measure of relative sweetness; this sweetener is several hundred times sweeter than sucrose
read as a comparison with table sugar, the clue describes an artificial sweetener

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like praise for someone extremely sweet-natured, but it is a literal chemical comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial sweetener roughly three to five hundred times sweeter than sucrose.

clue.text: A thirty-six-inch weapon? No, it's only part of a square sail.

parts.note: a yard is thirty-six inches
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: A comic question about a yard-long weapon, swiftly corrected to a piece of rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is the outer end of the spar from which a square sail hangs, so it belongs to that rig.

clue.text: The way you might exit a highway takes time to really get your dander up!

indicators.note: the first piece takes, adds on, the next piece after it

parts.words: The way you might exit a highway
parts.note: an exit ramp, or off-ramp, leads off a highway
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Leaving the freeway takes so long it makes you furious.
explanation.walkthrough: To get your dander up is to lose your temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To rampage is to rush about in a violent frenzy, the action of someone thoroughly enraged.

clue.text: A real meddler, to cause damage to an area of land.

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a plot is a piece of ground

explanation.surface: A busybody who goes out of their way to spoil a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A marplot is a person whose interference spoils a plan, an officious meddler.

clue.text: Indulging in scathing parody, Critias gets all mixed up.

indicators.note: a name that gets all mixed up has its letters jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the name Critias is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Critias, the Athenian figure, becomes confused while mocking others.
explanation.walkthrough: Critias was an ancient Athenian politician and writer, a fitting name for a classical satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiric writing ridicules its targets through parody and mockery, so it indulges in scathing parody.

clue.text: What goes around the middle, perhaps, to say incorrectly how one makes certain dance steps.

parts.words: What goes around the middle, perhaps
parts.note: a sash is a band worn around the waist, one example of such a thing

indicators.note: say incorrectly means the letters of say are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the word say is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A belt, and someone describing dance steps badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sashay comes from the French chassé, a gliding ballroom step.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to perform a chassé, the gliding sideways step in square and ballroom dancing.

clue.text: A genuine high spot offered by the land salesman.

parts.note: real means genuine, not fake
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: An estate agent shows off a real hilltop viewpoint on a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A realtor is the American term for an estate agent, who sells land and houses.

clue.text: The sort of mush that says what the singer does if she can't recall the words!

definitions.text: what the singer does if she can't recall the words
definitions.note: a clause standing for a third-person verb: she does this

indicators.note: a sort of mush is a jumbled version of the word, rearranged

parts.note: the word mush is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A sentimental, mushy song whose singer has forgotten the lyrics.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer who forgets the lyrics carries the tune with closed lips, vocalising without words.

clue.text: Said to cause a certain amount of waste.

definitions.text: Said to cause a certain amount of waste.

parts.note: said as in proverbially said, pointing to a well-known saying

parts.words: cause a certain amount of waste
parts.note: recalls the proverb that hurrying carelessly makes for wasted effort

explanation.walkthrough: Said looks like a sound-alike signal, but here it points to the proverb 'more haste, less speed', or 'haste makes waste'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'haste makes waste' says that rushing leads to mistakes and wasted effort.

clue.text: A "meat and potatoes"-plus dish? You might stand Pat for it.

definitions.text: A "meat and potatoes"-plus dish? You might stand Pat for it.

parts.note: the dish is a simple braise of mutton, potatoes and onions, so meat and potatoes plus a little more
Pat is a stock nickname for an Irishman, and to stand someone a meal is to treat them to it

explanation.surface: A hearty dish described, then a hint of a poker player standing pat.
explanation.walkthrough: Stand pat is poker talk for keeping one's hand, but here stand means buy for, and Pat is the Irishman. The answer continues at 3-down.
explanation.definitionFit: This classic stew of mutton, potatoes and onion is the national dish of Ireland.

clue.text: Some say things will come out in it. Shaw might be responsible for a sort of this!

definitions.text: Some say things will come out in it.
definitions.note: the saying 'it will all come out in the wash' means the truth emerges in the end

indicators.note: a sort of Shaw is that name in some other arrangement

parts.note: the name Shaw is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A proverb about secrets emerging, then George Bernard Shaw blamed for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom 'it will all come out in the wash'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laundering removes stains, so stains come out in it, and the idiom says the truth emerges eventually.

clue.text: What the young vocal artist does these days is brought up here–but one might do it in the ring.

definitions.text: one might do it in the ring

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing a word up reads it from bottom to top

parts.words: What the young vocal artist does these days
parts.note: modern young performers rap, chanting rhythmic lyrics

explanation.surface: Young singers today rap, and that gets mentioned here alongside a boxer's routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers spar in the ring, practising with light punches against a partner.

clue.text: It could be a bit of noise from your engine, but "pong" makes it game!

definitions.text: It could be a bit of noise from your engine, but "pong" makes it game!

parts.words: a bit of noise from your engine
parts.note: a sharp metallic knocking from an engine is called by this name
put the word pong after the answer and you get the hyphenated name of table tennis

explanation.surface: Engine noises, and how a second sound would turn one into a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinging is the metallic knock of an engine pre-igniting, and with pong added it names table tennis.

clue.text: What's found on top with transportation in Chicago? It may be essential to the operation!

definitions.text: It may be essential to the operation!

parts.note: the scalp is the skin on top of the head
the El is Chicago's elevated railway

explanation.surface: A riddle about Chicago transit that turns out to concern surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Operation looks like a business or transit operation; here it is surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is the surgeon's small blade, a basic tool in any surgical procedure.

clue.text: A pilot article by way of a high spot.

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
via means by way of
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A trial piece of writing routed over a peak, like a pilot episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Pilot article looks like a trial publication; here pilot is the definition. A tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is someone who flies aircraft, the same as a pilot.

clue.text: Evidently the top officer, in short, gives an evaluation–but one damns the result!

definitions.note: a clause standing for a third-person verb: one who does this damns

parts.note: exec is short for executive, the top officer of a company
rates means assesses or gives a rating

explanation.surface: A senior officer issues an appraisal, and someone curses the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or denounce bitterly, which is to damn.

clue.text: A bridge expert may be right, but has gone wrong about it!

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit about, around, the short piece
gone wrong means the letters of gone are out of order, rearranged

parts.note: the word gone is taken as written and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A bridge expert may be correct but has blundered over something.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Goren was the famous American bridge player and writer whose bidding system dominated the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Goren was the leading American authority on contract bridge in the mid twentieth century.
